_about: Component spec for pos-slider — created 2026-10-06 from the approved component-wizard draft via scripts/generate-component.js. Single source of truth for the Variants/Usage/Tokens tabs on /style-guide. One variant; the value bubble is the Tooltip component's look — declared via composedOf, its tokens live on the Tooltip panel (RULES.md 7.12); states normal and focus (keyboard focus ring on the input). Behavior (fill + value tooltip follow the input) lives in assets/js/pos-slider.js, loaded by init. Figma names resolved through pos-config.css (RULES.md §6.4). Regenerate spec-slider.liquid after any change here — never hand-edit the .liquid partial.
name: Slider
description: Picks a value from a range (0–100 by default) by dragging a handle along a track — a real <input type="range">, so keyboard and screen readers work out of the box. The filled part shows the value; while dragging, a tooltip above the handle shows the number.
whenToUse: Choosing an approximate value from a continuous range where the position matters more than the exact number (volume, opacity, a percentage).
Giving immediate visual feedback while the value changes.
whenNotToUse: The user needs to enter an exact number — use a text input (type="number").
There are only a few distinct options — use a segmented control, radio buttons or a select.
The range is very large (e.g. 0–10 000) — a small handle can't pick precise values; use an input.
do: Give it a visible label (or at least an aria-label) that says what is being set.
Show the current value next to the slider too when it matters after letting go — the tooltip only shows while dragging.
Keep the default range 0–100 unless the context needs another one (set min / max / step on the input).
dont: Use a slider for an on / off choice — use a toggle button.
Hide the track or the fill — the filled part is how the value is read at a glance.
Make it narrower than about 160px — the handle needs room to move.
accessibility: It is a native range input: arrow keys, Page Up / Down, Home / End and screen readers work without extra code; label it with <label for> or aria-label.
The value tooltip is visual only (aria-hidden) — the input itself announces its value.
The keyboard focus ring sits on the input (the regular DS focus color).

props.name: min / max / step / value
props.description: The native range input attributes; the module reads them for the fill and the value tooltip.

props.name: --ratio
props.description: 0–1, where the handle is; the JS module keeps it in sync with the input — set it in the markup too, so the fill is right before the JS runs.
